paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take from this one, friend. Balak summoned Balaam to curse Israel, and he got a blessing three times in a row. Balaam says it plainly: he "could not do anything of my own accord, good or bad, to go beyond the command of the LORD" (Numbers 24:13). When God has said bless, no hilltop, no king and no house full of silver and gold can flip it.

Now look at what Balaam says about Israel: "Blessed are those who bless you and cursed are those who curse you" (Numbers 24:9). That promise is bigger than one bad day in Moab. Then he looks way down the road and says, "A star will come forth from Jacob, and a scepter will arise from Israel" (Numbers 24:17). I think that's the part to hold onto, because God was already working on something good long before anybody in that camp could see it.

And the story isn't over, baker. Balaam asks, "Ah, who can live unless God has ordained it?" (Numbers 24:23), and the nations he names come and go. God's word is the one thing that stands. So when the news is loud and the plans of people look big, keep your ovens warm and stay in the Word, because what God has said is what will happen.
